findings.title: Manifestation becomes harmful exposure
findings.claim: The first disclosure is not merely the arrival of information; it is a making-visible that can expose the addressees to harm.
findings.mechanism: The passive disclosure form names something becoming manifest, and the following direct distress verb supplies the harmful consequence of that exposure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear why disclosure itself is dangerous in this conditional, before any broader interpretation is added.
findings.containment: This retains the ordinary disclosure sense and does not claim that every manifestation is harmful.

epistemic.reason: The supplied word-analysis support states the manifestation-to-exposure relation directly.

findings.title: Agentless disclosure
findings.claim: The first conditional foregrounds disclosure while leaving the discloser unspoken.
findings.mechanism: The passive jussive form is governed by the first conditional, so the matters appear as what is made visible and the agent is suppressed on the surface.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning feels like a described event that can befall the audience, not like an explanation of who performs it.
findings.containment: The omitted agent is a grammatical foregrounding effect, not a claim that no agent exists.

epistemic.reason: The supplied morphology and word analysis agree on passive agency suppression.

findings.containment: The phrase still marks recipients; the disadvantage is a contextual pressure supplied by its contact with the harm clause.
